hero.alt: An accelerated coding stage tilts the delivery chain while people support the downstream work.
hero.caption: Machine-speed production does not automatically expand the capacity needed to own the result.
hero.credit: Author-selected AI-assisted editorial illustration from the R2 kit.

asymmetry.alt: A conceptual orange curve for potential AI task pace rises above a teal curve for effective human and organisational capacity across seven lifecycle stages. The shaded gap represents pressure to rebalance; no values are measured.
asymmetry.caption: Figure 1. Speed asymmetry across the lifecycle. Curve heights and gaps are illustrative, not measured values, rankings or throughput estimates.
asymmetry.credit: Original explanatory diagram by Vitalii Oborskyi, developed from the supplied infographic.

workstream-system.alt: Seven delivery activities connect to outcomes and a feedback path. Beneath them are six enabling relationships: dependencies, learning, decision rights, capacity, ownership and recovery.
workstream-system.caption: Figure 2. The workstream is one view of the delivery system. Its results depend on relationships and capabilities that the arrows alone do not show.
workstream-system.credit: Original explanatory diagram by Vitalii Oborskyi, developed from the supplied infographic.

review-functions.alt: Four review functions reported by Bacchelli and Bird—defect detection, knowledge transfer, team awareness and alternative solutions—sit above the operational capabilities to explain, diagnose, intervene and recover.
review-functions.caption: Figure 3. Review functions and operational capabilities are distinct. Automation can change the practice; the necessary functions still need a working mechanism.
review-functions.credit: Original explanatory diagram by Vitalii Oborskyi. Top functions: Bacchelli and Bird (2013); extension to ownership and recovery: author systems synthesis.

imbalance-loop.alt: Admitted work above effective capacity can increase interruptions and overload for people, fragility and change costs for products, and rework and ownership costs for business. Repair consumes improvement capacity and reinforces the overload.
imbalance-loop.caption: Figure 4. How overload can move costs across people, product and business. A conditional risk mechanism, not an inevitable forecast.
imbalance-loop.credit: Original explanatory diagram by Vitalii Oborskyi, developed from the supplied infographic and the R2 overload mechanism.

systemic-response.alt: An accountable owner supports a four-step feedback loop: frame the problem, test a hypothesis, evaluate system outcomes, then keep, change or stop. Evidence can send the organisation back to its original diagnosis.
systemic-response.caption: Figure 5. A systemic response is a learning loop. Authority and resources make the owner effective; evidence can change both the intervention and the problem statement.
systemic-response.credit: Original explanatory diagram by Vitalii Oborskyi, developed from the supplied infographic.
